* *Serilog Integration and Testing (1.5 hrs):*

* *Deployment and Validation (1.5 hrs):*

** Tested system behavior and confirmed that logs were generated and accessible.
** Troubleshot some latency issues due to local laptop performance, which delayed progress.
* *Elasticsearch Index Planning (1.5 hrs):*

** Designed a basic indexing plan suited for the project log structure.
** Outlined ideas for future enhancements like structured log fields and searchable tags.

fields.summary: Apply elastic search to log changes

worklogs.comment:
# *Setup & Learned Elasticsearch 9.x*
#* Understood basic concepts: Cluster, Node, Index, Document.
#* Installed Elasticsearch and Kibana via Docker.
# *Integrated Elasticsearch with .NET*
#* Used {{Elastic.Clients.Elasticsearch}} NuGet package for modern, strong-typed access.
#* Connected to Elasticsearch with/without API key authentication.
# *Defined an Audit Log Data Model*
#* Created {{AuditLogEntry}} DTO with: Entity, EntityId, Field, Action, OldValue, NewValue, User, Timestamp.
# *Captured Changes from EF Core*
#* Built an extension method ({{CaptureAuditLogEntries}}) to extract all changes per Save (create/update/delete).
#* Ensured changes are captured for all entities and tables in a generic, reusable way.
# *Implemented Fire-and-Forget Logging*
#* Built a background queue ({{IAuditLogQueue}} + implementation) so audit logging does NOT block main DB saves.
#* Used batch (bulk) indexing for performance and reliability.
# *ElasticSearch Bulk Indexing per Entity*
#* Logs stored in per-entity indices (e.g., {{auditlog-company}}, {{auditlog-calender}}).
#* Enables fast, filtered queries by {{EntityId}} for any entity/table.
# *Query Audit History Efficiently*
#* Added service method to fetch audit history by entity and master ID.
#* Supported robust querying compatible with various field mappings.
# *Diagnosed and Fixed Field Mapping Issues*
#* Verified data and mappings in Kibana Dev Tools.
#* Adjusted query style ({{term}} vs {{match}}) for best compatibility.
# *Kibana Integration*
#* Set up index patterns and discovered logs in Kibana UI.
#* Used Dev Tools for advanced troubleshooting.

* Arranged and participated in a meeting to discuss strategies for integrating Elasticsearch indexing and data insertion with the team.
* Collected requirements and clarifications from TL, especially regarding logging behavior: specifically, logging directly to Elasticsearch rather than relying on EF Core’s {{SaveChanges}}.
* Began prototyping a method to capture and log request and response data for API endpoints, aligning with new requirements (not using old methods for historical logs).

* Focused on implementing and testing audit log capture for several endpoints, specifically around Calendar and Holiday modules.
* Ongoing: Working to resolve blockers in request/response logging and optimizing the logging workflow per the discussed strategy.

# *Deep-dive Research on Elasticsearch Audit Logging*
#* Compared best practices for index-per-entity vs index-per-page audit log design.
#* Validated that using one index per entity/page is optimal for ERP audit logs.
# *Elasticsearch Index/Mapping Analysis* 
#* Analyzed existing Elasticsearch index mappings using Kibana Dev Tools.
#* Investigated mapping conflicts, especially object vs string issues (e.g., {{"path"}} field).
#* Verified correct storage of {{entityId}}, {{requestBody}}, and {{responseBody}} fields.
# *Elasticsearch Query Troubleshooting & R&D* 
#* Tested multiple query types ({{term}}, {{match}}) against stored audit log data.
#* Identified root cause of empty search results due to mapping differences (e.g., {{entityId}} as {{text}}).
#* Documented query strategies based on mapping ({{.keyword}} vs direct field).
# *.NET Integration & Code Refactoring* 
#* Refactored the logging pipeline to use a single index per page/entity for audit logs.
#* Implemented new {{IndexSingleLogAsync}} and {{GetHistoryAsync}} methods for efficient storage and retrieval.
#* Ensured all audit logs include a stable {{entityId}} property for history search.
# *Serialization and Data Consistency Fixes* 
#* Identified and resolved issues where {{requestBody}}/{{responseBody}} were being stored as JSON strings, not objects.
#* Improved log object building in .NET to guarantee properties are stored as structured objects for Elasticsearch, not as JSON strings.
# *Mapping Conflict Resolution* 
#* Debugged and fixed mapping conflict with the {{"path"}} field (object vs string).
#* Documented solution: all future logs must use a consistent type for {{"path"}}; index recreation if type needs to change.
# *Testing & Verification in Kibana* 
#* Indexed sample logs and confirmed data format using Kibana Dev Tools.
#* Verified document structure, field names, and query behavior.
# *Discussion & Documentation* 
#* Discussed blockers and findings on storing request/response bodies.
#* Documented design decisions, best practices, and limitations (e.g., Elasticsearch does not support dynamic field type changes).

----

h3. *Pending/Blockers*

* *[BLOCKER]* Current implementation saves {{requestBody}} and {{responseBody}} as JSON strings, not objects, due to C# serialization limitations with anonymous/dynamic types.
** Need further R&D or refactor to always store these fields as structured objects for better query and usability.
** *Solution options:*
*** Use strongly-typed DTOs instead of anonymous objects.
*** Update log creation to avoid double-serialization.
* *HistoryService Refactoring (In Progress)*
** Major refactoring required to handle new audit log structure.
** Must support deserializing stored JSON strings for backward compatibility.
** Further work needed to adapt the retrieval logic and parsing in the UI/service layer.
* *Index Mapping Cleanup*
** Pending: Plan for index re-creation or mapping templates to ensure future fields (like {{path}}) are consistently typed.

*Note:*
The code implemented during this R&D phase is intended as a proof-of-concept/sample and does not fully follow company coding standards or best practices.

My primary goal was to validate the end-to-end integration of Elasticsearch and the new audit/history logging workflow, ensure correct data flow, and identify/eliminate major blockers.

Once the correct architecture and flow are confirmed, I will refactor and implement production-quality code in a new branch, following all coding standards and best practices.



*Branch Information:*
All work for Elasticsearch R&D and audit logging is being developed on branch:

{{develop/platform/sprint-26/OBPP-4/elastic-search/dileepa/OBPP-3833/OBPP-4461/Apply-elastic-search }}

This branch contains all experiments, sample implementations, and integration work for the new Elasticsearch audit log module.

*Working Style:*

* I am pushing all changes to remote every 30 minutes, ensuring transparency and traceability.
* Anyone can review my latest code and progress in this branch at any time.
* Once the integration and workflow are fully validated, production-quality code will be refactored and committed in a separate branch according to company coding standards.

* Investigated and implemented ElasticSearch-based history/audit logging for ERP master and transaction forms.
* Developed and tested logic to store and retrieve detailed change history (including handling large response bodies with 5000+ words per record).
* Compared ElasticSearch to Loki for log storage—found that ES can handle large text bodies, but Loki has limitations with long logs.
* Collaborated with Frontend (FE) to clarify requirements and align response formats, especially for relationship-based history logs.
* Spent additional time troubleshooting laptop slowness which impacted my productivity during the day.
* Tested end-to-end: saved large payloads to ES, verified storage and retrieval, and checked integration with FE’s expectations for audit trail.
* Paused on advanced nested comparison logic for now (pending further discussion) to ensure the base solution works for both main and related entities.
* Some time spent analyzing request samples and researching optimal JSON property extraction methods for accurate change tracking.
* Work is still *R&D/prototype*—current code is not fully production-ready, will refactor and standardize in the next branch after core functionality is finalized.
